SOIL-U1-L01.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U1-L01.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: A learner is asked to enter a field sprayed yesterday. The product label and re-entry instruction are unavailable. No entry decision has been confirmed by the supervisor.
SIMULATED CASE B: A stopped tiller has a cracked, partly detached protective guard. A colleague suggests using extra PPE to finish a short task.
Identify the hazard, exposure and first control for each case. State what information or action is required before work can begin.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U1-L01.evidence: Two justified go/no-go decisions and a task-specific protection list.
SOIL-U1-L01.feedback: Check that your decisions control the hazard before relying on PPE and do not invent a re-entry interval.

SOIL-U1-L02.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U1-L02.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: An adult operator notices a fuel leak while a small tiller is running. You are outside the machine's work area and have a phone. You have not been trained to repair the fuel system.
SIMULATED CASE B: A colleague in a hot field reports dizziness and appears confused. You do not know the cause. The trainer and local emergency plan are available.
For each case, explain how to protect yourself, alert the responsible person and report the location. Limit actions to your training and the emergency plan.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U1-L02.evidence: A short spoken or written emergency report and an explanation of safe boundaries.
SOIL-U1-L02.feedback: Check for clear location and hazard information. Do not add an improvised rescue, diagnosis or treatment.

SOIL-U1-L04.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U1-L04.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: Sample A is a supplied simulation: gritty feel, little cohesion after moistening, no ribbon observed. Its light-brown color was recorded under the same lighting as the other cases.
SIMULATED CASE B: Sample B is a supplied simulation: smooth and slightly gritty feel, with a weak short ribbon observed. No laboratory particle-size result is available.

Compare the observations and suggest provisional texture groups with uncertainty. State what extra guide or measurement you would use. Do not invent ribbon lengths or infer crops, salinity or fertility.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U1-L04.evidence: A learner response comparing the supplied observations, provisional interpretation and missing evidence.
SOIL-U1-L04.feedback: Check that no short ribbon is treated as proof of loam and no color is treated as a measured nutrient result. Real ribbon testing is a separate trainer-observed task.

SOIL-U1-L05.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U1-L05.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: Container A-01 and its field form both identify Zone A, the same collection date and the same specified depth. The laboratory's written handling instruction is attached.
SIMULATED CASE B: Container B-02 is accompanied by a form labelled B-03. The intended test and handling instruction are missing. No one can confirm the identity from memory.
Check traceability and decide what can be handed over. List the clarification needed for each uncertain field. Do not change an identifier or invent a handling temperature.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U1-L05.evidence: An error log and a justified handover decision for each sample.
SOIL-U1-L05.feedback: Check identity before interpreting results. Handling must follow the receiving laboratory's test-specific instruction.

SOIL-U1-L06.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U1-L06.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: Method Record A defines one management zone, purpose, date, specified depth, planned point distribution, clean tools and the laboratory handling instructions.
SIMULATED CASE B: Method Record B says only 'soil was collected near the gate'. It gives no depth, zone boundary, point count, tool condition or handling information.
Compare reproducibility. Explain why each missing field matters and write questions to obtain it. Do not supply imaginary collection details.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U1-L06.evidence: A revised method template with unknown fields clearly marked.
SOIL-U1-L06.feedback: Check that the template records the real method and limitations rather than copying the pilot's sample numbers.

SOIL-U1-L07.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U1-L07.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: Practice Record A has a matching map and container identifier, but its handling method is not recorded. No trainer observation has yet been entered.
SIMULATED CASE B: Practice Record B describes good sampling knowledge in an online answer, but there is no evidence that the learner performed the field task.
Identify which criteria remain unverified and plan the trainer-observed demonstration. These supplied records are simulations, not evidence of your own competence.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U1-L07.evidence: A checklist of required observations, missing information and a reassessment plan.
SOIL-U1-L07.feedback: Knowledge answers and practical evidence are separate. Unobserved criteria remain unobserved until the trainer checks them.

SOIL-U2-L01.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U2-L01.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: A crop shows pale leaves. The case gives no soil-test interpretation, crop stage, moisture record or root observations.
SIMULATED CASE B: A second crop has slow growth and visibly damaged roots in saturated soil. No nutrient deficiency has been confirmed.
Describe possible explanations and choose useful next observations or tests. Explain nutrient roles without selecting a fertilizer dose.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U2-L01.evidence: Two evidence-gathering plans with provisional hypotheses.
SOIL-U2-L01.feedback: Do not turn an appearance into a confirmed diagnosis. Check root and water conditions as well as nutrient evidence.

SOIL-U2-L02.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U2-L02.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: Case A has dry soil around otherwise visible roots. The supplied record says nutrients are present, but gives no measurement of transport or uptake.
SIMULATED CASE B: Case B has compacted soil and a restricted root system. Its reported nutrient supply is similar to Case A.
Use mass flow, diffusion and root interception to explain why uptake might be restricted differently. State the observations needed to test your explanation.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U2-L02.evidence: A mechanism-based comparison that distinguishes nutrient presence from access.
SOIL-U2-L02.feedback: Do not claim one mechanism acts alone or invent a transport speed, uptake rate or fertilizer remedy.

SOIL-U2-L03.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U2-L03.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: Pale plants occur mainly in a saturated low area. A supplied observation records damaged roots, while the cause of the leaf color remains unconfirmed.
SIMULATED CASE B: Another group has pale older leaves in a different field area. There is no matching soil or plant analysis and no complete irrigation record.
Build at least two provisional hypotheses for each case. Name future observations or tests to obtain that would distinguish them; do not claim those future results were already observed.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U2-L03.evidence: A diagnostic comparison with evidence for, evidence missing and next step.
SOIL-U2-L03.feedback: Check that neither case is automatically labelled nitrogen deficiency and that you do not prescribe treatment from the photograph-like description.

SOIL-U2-L04.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U2-L04.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: Sample A has a simulated pH of 5.5 measured by Method M. The sample identity and Method M are recorded.
SIMULATED CASE B: Sample B has a simulated pH of 8.0 measured by the same Method M. No salinity, sodium or lime-requirement result is supplied.
Compare relative acidity or alkalinity and explain what cannot be inferred from these values. Treat the figures as training data.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U2-L04.evidence: A short interpretation that separates pH from salinity, nutrient concentration and treatment rate.
SOIL-U2-L04.feedback: Check the logarithmic meaning without converting the pH difference into an amendment dose.

SOIL-U2-L05.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U2-L05.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: Record A: sample A-01, laboratory Method M, calibration completed and recorded according to the meter instructions, two simulated readings of 6.3 and 6.4. The procedure's repeatability acceptance limit is not supplied.
SIMULATED CASE B: Record B: sample B-01, simulated reading 6.5, but no preparation method or calibration record.
Assess documentation and identify what must be confirmed before accepting either result. Do not invent an acceptance tolerance.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U2-L05.evidence: A measurement-quality review with missing information and next checks.
SOIL-U2-L05.feedback: A plausible reading is not proof of valid measurement. Acceptance depends on the specified procedure and quality criteria.

SOIL-U2-L06.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U2-L06.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: An acidic soil report gives simulated pH 5.5 but no lime-requirement test, crop target or amendment specification.
SIMULATED CASE B: A second report mentions high conductivity but omits the extraction method, sodium information and drainage conditions.
Explain why neither report supports an immediate universal lime or gypsum dose. Identify the evidence needed for a conditional recommendation.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U2-L06.evidence: A decision note listing the missing tests, crop context and responsible adviser.
SOIL-U2-L06.feedback: Keep acidity, salinity and sodicity distinct. Do not prescribe a treatment merely because its name is familiar.

SOIL-U2-L07.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U2-L07.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: The laboratory's simulated instruction for Sample A requests routine fertility preparation by its specified air-drying procedure.
SIMULATED CASE B: The laboratory's simulated instruction for Sample B requests fresh material for a biological test, with chilled transport under a separate written protocol.
Plan separate preparation and labeling paths using the supplied instructions. List additional equipment or protocol details to confirm before practical work.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U2-L07.evidence: A preparation plan showing sample identity, assigned method, contamination controls and quality checks.
SOIL-U2-L07.feedback: Do not apply air-drying or chilling to both samples automatically. Real execution requires the trainer and the complete laboratory procedure.

SOIL-U2-L08.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U2-L08.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: The supplied Kit A result for phosphorus is Medium on its own Low/Medium/High scale. Its written procedure provides no conversion from those categories to a concentration.

SIMULATED CASE B: The supplied Report B states organic matter 2.1% by laboratory method OM-1. The copy omits both the method details and its quality-control record. This is training data, not a measurement made by the learner.
Explain how you would record Kit A without inventing ppm and what you would request before relying on Report B.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U2-L08.evidence: A methods-and-limitations table for the two supplied results.
SOIL-U2-L08.feedback: Record Kit A as Medium under its own scale, with no invented concentration. Request the missing method details and quality-control evidence for Report B before interpreting it. Keep reported data separate from a judgement about soil quality.

SOIL-U2-L09.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U2-L09.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: A simulated jar model has three measured teaching layers of 2 cm, 3 cm and 5 cm, for a total sediment height of 10 cm. These are model layer heights, not laboratory particle-size masses.
SIMULATED CASE B: A second simulated jar has cloudy liquid and boundaries that cannot be identified reliably.
Calculate layer-height percentages for the first model and explain why the second should not receive invented measurements. Do not treat either as certified texture analysis.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U2-L09.evidence: A worked calculation and an uncertainty note.
SOIL-U2-L09.feedback: Show each layer divided by the stated total. Keep the interpretation limited to the instructional model.

SOIL-U2-L10.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U2-L10.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: Training Dataset A: 40% sand, 40% silt and 20% clay, measured on the same basis. This is a simulated example.
SIMULATED CASE B: Training Dataset B: 55% sand, 30% silt and 20% clay. The supplied total is inconsistent and no correction is authorized.
Check each total. Use the USDA triangle or referenced calculator only for the valid dataset, and flag the other for clarification.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U2-L10.evidence: The arithmetic, the valid classification and a justified rejection of the inconsistent input.
SOIL-U2-L10.feedback: Dataset A is the checked loam example. Do not force Dataset B to sum correctly by silently changing a value.

SOIL-U2-L11.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U2-L11.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: Report A links sample A-01 to its field form and states pH 6.4 by Method M, but lists conductivity 2.1 without a unit or extraction method. All values are simulated.
SIMULATED CASE B: Report B contains a texture class but a container identifier that differs from the field record. No resolution is supplied.
Write a results table that preserves known data and visibly flags missing units, methods and identity problems. Do not interpret the uncertain conductivity or repair the identity by guessing.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U2-L11.evidence: A corrected report layout and a clarification log.
SOIL-U2-L11.feedback: Separate data transcription from interpretation. A well-formatted table does not make an unidentified sample reliable.

SOIL-U2-L12.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U2-L12.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: A simulated field record gives a provisional texture estimate and pH, but does not provide water quality, crop demand or laboratory amendment guidance.
SIMULATED CASE B: A proposed plan recommends one fixed fertilizer dose and promises a yield increase without showing its evidence.
Assess the plan, propose a conditional next step and list the information needed before an application recommendation.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U2-L12.evidence: A preliminary advice note with evidence, limitations and monitoring.
SOIL-U2-L12.feedback: Do not replace one unsupported dose with another. A justified request for information is an acceptable outcome.

SOIL-U2-L13.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U2-L13.task: Compare the two supplied simulated learner-evidence profiles. Decide which skills still need assessment, and check the supplied arithmetic. These profiles contain all the facts needed for this task; they are not field data or laboratory operating instructions.
steps: SIMULATED PROFILE A | Learner: A | Written knowledge check: 4 correct out of 4 | Interpretation assignment: meets stated criteria | Direct observation of sample handling: not yet done | Direct observation of meter use: not yet done | Practical competence decision: pending. Decide whether the written results establish the unobserved practical skills.

SIMULATED PROFILE B | Learner: B | Sample identification: observed correctly by trainer | Eye protection: observed correctly | Probe rinsing: observed correctly | Recorded sediment-layer values: 2, 2, 1 | Recorded total: 6 | Units: not recorded | Correction or explanation: absent. The layer values are for checking this learner record, not real soil measurements.

For Profile A, name the missing type of evidence and the practical observations to arrange. For Profile B, calculate the sum, identify what prevents interpretation of the values, and state which reporting/calculation criteria need reassessment. Keep the satisfactory observations separate from the unresolved criteria.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U2-L13.feedback: Case A still needs direct observation of the practical skills. In Case B, the listed layers sum to 5, not 6, and the units must be confirmed. Keep the recorded practical observations separate from the calculation error and target reassessment at the actual gaps.

SOIL-U3-L01.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U3-L01.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: The supplied crop list is maize, common bean, tomato and a fodder grass. Sort by the practical product/use categories discussed in the lesson and explain possible overlap.
SIMULATED CASE B: The same crops are also to be considered for a rotation. Their botanical relationships and relevant shared pest risks must be checked before making that decision.
Explain why a market category and a botanical group answer different questions. Do not claim that a legume always provides a fixed nitrogen credit.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U3-L01.evidence: A classification table naming the criterion used and the limits of each grouping.
SOIL-U3-L01.feedback: Check that group labels are useful for the stated decision rather than treated as a complete production recommendation.

SOIL-U3-L02.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U3-L02.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: Simulated Site A is described as deep, adequately drained loam with a reliable water supply. Crop variety and seasonal climate information are missing.
SIMULATED CASE B: Simulated Site B has the same texture label but shallow rooting and persistent wetness. Its water quality has not been tested.
Compare the sites and identify what else is needed before choosing a crop. Do not assume equal texture means equal suitability.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U3-L02.evidence: A conditional suitability comparison and an information request list.
SOIL-U3-L02.feedback: Include soil, climate, variety and water. Avoid promising a crop or yield from the texture label alone.

SOIL-U3-L03.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U3-L03.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: Rotation Option A uses tomato followed by pepper; the exercise supplies that both are in the Solanaceae family. The local pest situation is unknown.
SIMULATED CASE B: Rotation Option B uses a legume followed by a cereal; water requirements, planting windows and actual nitrogen contribution have not been established.
Compare the reasoning behind the options, identify uncertainties and propose checks before selecting a sequence.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U3-L03.evidence: A rotation discussion linking purpose, family, resources and monitoring.
SOIL-U3-L03.feedback: Neither option is automatically ideal. Do not assume a family change solves every pest problem or a legume supplies a fixed fertilizer saving.

SOIL-U3-L04.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U3-L04.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: Simulated Crop A is wilted in dry soil, with no recent irrigation recorded.
SIMULATED CASE B: Simulated Crop B is also wilted, but the soil is saturated and the supplied observation notes damaged roots.
Explain different possible mechanisms and the next observations needed. Do not assign the same watering response from leaf appearance alone.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U3-L04.feedback: Use soil and root evidence. Avoid universal watering intervals or treating all stored soil water as plant-available.

SOIL-U3-L05.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U3-L05.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: Irrigation Record A shows uneven wetting and a visible leak. Nutrient test interpretation has not been supplied.
SIMULATED CASE B: Plan B proposes increasing both irrigation and fertilizer without checking drainage, crop stage or existing nutrient supply.
Use the four-R questions and water-management evidence to review the plan. State what can be corrected or investigated before selecting rates.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U3-L05.evidence: A combined management review with missing evidence clearly identified.
SOIL-U3-L05.feedback: Do not invent an application rate. More water or fertilizer is not automatically the right response.

SOIL-U3-L06.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U3-L06.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: Report A gives an electrical-conductivity value from a saturation extract. Report B gives a value from a different soil-water extraction ratio. No valid conversion is provided.
SIMULATED CASE B: A field shows a pale surface crust and high pH, but no sodium or water-quality result is available.
Explain why the two conductivity numbers cannot be compared directly and why the field description does not establish sodicity by itself.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U3-L06.evidence: A method-aware salinity assessment and a list of required tests.
SOIL-U3-L06.feedback: Keep observation, measurement method and diagnosis distinct. Do not supply a treatment threshold without the relevant framework.

SOIL-U3-L07.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U3-L07.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: Plan A proposes mulch and a suitable organic input to address exposure and soil-structure concerns, subject to material quality and local management checks.
SIMULATED CASE B: Plan B proposes leaching an undrained field with water of unknown quality and adding gypsum without a sodium assessment.
Compare what evidence supports each plan, identify possible harms and list conditions needed before implementation.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U3-L07.evidence: A staged management proposal with monitoring and responsibilities.
SOIL-U3-L07.feedback: Do not assume a single product solves arid-soil constraints. Consider water quality, drainage and the actual diagnosed problem.

SOIL-U3-L08.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U3-L08.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: Site A has a supplied description of deep, well-drained sandy loam and reliable irrigation. The crop variety, season and water salinity are unknown.
SIMULATED CASE B: Site B has a clay-rich surface estimate and shallow rooting. Its drainage and available water have not been assessed.
Prepare a conditional crop-selection checklist for each site. Explain which information prevents a final recommendation.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U3-L08.evidence: A comparison of evidence, constraints and alternative pathways.
SOIL-U3-L08.feedback: Do not rank all sand as poor or all loam as ideal. Suitability depends on more than mineral texture.

SOIL-U3-L09.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U3-L09.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: A simulated report gives sample A-01, 40% sand, 40% silt, 20% clay and pH 6.4 by stated Method M. Field observations identify a shallow compacted layer; no salinity or water-quality result is supplied.
SIMULATED CASE B: A proposed recommendation calls the field ideal for every crop and specifies an amendment rate without further evidence.
Prepare a one-page preliminary review using the valid results, observed constraint and missing information. Reject unsupported universal claims.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U3-L09.evidence: A traceable report with conditional options and an evidence-gathering plan.
SOIL-U3-L09.feedback: Keep the dataset labelled simulated. Texture and pH do not erase the rooting constraint or determine an amendment dose.

SOIL-U3-L10.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U3-L10.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: The supplied component-function pairs are: clutch lever—controls drive engagement; drag bar—helps control tilling behavior/depth; protective guard—separates people from a hazard. Verify them against the linked FQ650 owner's manual.
SIMULATED CASE B: A proposed task uses a different attachment in a narrow planted row. Attachment compatibility and safe clearance have not been confirmed.
Explain the component functions and decide what must be checked before accepting the task. Use only stopped-machine observation for identification.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U3-L10.evidence: A component-function explanation and a go/no-go task assessment.
SOIL-U3-L10.feedback: Do not assume an accessory is compatible or that a conceptual picture shows the exact control position.

SOIL-U3-L11.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U3-L11.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: Precheck A finds a loose protective guard and a suspected fuel leak on a stopped FQ650. Someone suggests starting briefly to see whether the problem disappears.
SIMULATED CASE B: Precheck B has no reported defect, but the operator is not trained and the work area has not been cleared.
Explain why readiness is not established in either case. List the conditions that the trainer must verify before any powered demonstration.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U3-L11.evidence: A pre-operation decision record. Actual starting is a separate authorized adult demonstration under supervision.
SOIL-U3-L11.feedback: Do not start to diagnose an unsafe defect or treat an online explanation as operating permission.

SOIL-U3-L12.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U3-L12.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: Case A: the engine has just been stopped and is still hot. Refueling is proposed immediately.
SIMULATED CASE B: Case B: material is caught near the tines. The clutch has been released, but the engine remains running.
State the safe boundaries and required shutdown/isolation checks from the matching manual. Do not perform the simulated task on a live machine.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U3-L12.evidence: A stop, isolate and refer decision sequence with a maintenance-record template.
SOIL-U3-L12.feedback: Distinguish clutch release from safe isolation. Refueling and maintenance must follow the manual and trained supervision.

SOIL-U3-L13.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U3-L13.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: Planning Case A provides a matched sample identity, simulated texture and pH results with methods, and a note that water quality remains unknown.
SIMULATED CASE B: Planning Case B contains a mismatched sample identifier and unobserved practical criteria despite a completed report.
Plan how the final assessment should obtain valid individual evidence. For interpretation, keep the supplied data separate from measurements you will actually make.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U3-L13.evidence: A practical assessment plan and a preliminary report structure. Actual competence requires the assessor's observation.
SOIL-U3-L13.feedback: Do not copy simulation values into a real result sheet or claim a pass for unobserved work.

SOIL-U3-L14.title: Case comparison and justified decisions
SOIL-U3-L14.task: Use the supplied simulated cases for an online reasoning exercise. They are not observations from your fieldwork.
steps: SIMULATED CASE A: Reflection Record A shows strong written explanation but no observed field demonstration.
SIMULATED CASE B: Reflection Record B shows safe preparation but a missed calibration step and incomplete method recording.
Identify the specific gap in each record and propose targeted practice and reassessment, then compare the process with your own verified feedback.
Write your response in the activity box. Distinguish supplied facts, assumptions and missing evidence.
SOIL-U3-L14.evidence: A focused improvement plan naming support, evidence and review point.
SOIL-U3-L14.feedback: Do not repeat everything without purpose or convert confidence into competence. Reassessment outcomes belong to the assessor.
